stages.title: Advanced vocabulary and terminology
stages.hook: News in Japan often talks about 少子高齢化 and 持続可能. How do long compounds hold so much meaning?
explain: Advanced Japanese vocabulary is rich in kanji compounds. 経済 (keizai, economy), 環境 (kankyō, environment), 技術 (gijutsu, technology), 政策 (seisaku, policy) and 課題 (kadai, issue) appear in news and exams. Compounds can be long: 少子高齢化 (shōshi kōreika) means a falling birth rate and an ageing population.

Suffixes help you decode new words: 〜化 (-ka) means -ification (高齢化, ageing), 〜性 (-sei) means -ness (多様性, diversity), and 〜的 (-teki) makes an adjective (経済的, economic). 持続可能 (jizoku kanō) means sustainable, made from "continue" and "possible".
Collocations matter: 課題に取り組む (to tackle an issue), 環境を守る (to protect the environment), 政策を打ち出す (to put forward a policy). Learn the verb with the noun, and note whether the style is formal.
stages.mnemonic: Break compounds: 少子 + 高齢 + 化.
sentences: A declining birthrate and ageing is a big issue.

o: Means "not", like the prefix in 不安

gq.q: Which verb often goes with 課題?
gq.why: 課題に取り組む means to tackle an issue.

panel.q: How can 持続可能 be decoded?
panel.why: It combines 持続 (continue) and 可能 (possible).

panel.q: What does 多様性 refer to?
panel.why: 性 makes an abstract noun: diversity.

panel.q: Why learn 環境を守る as a unit?
o: Because 守る is a noun in this phrase
Because it is a particle that cannot be split
Because 環境 is a verb meaning to protect
panel.why: Collocations show natural word partners.

teach.model: Many advanced words are kanji compounds. Suffixes such as 化, 性 and 的 help you decode them. Learn nouns with their typical verbs.

points.ask: What should I learn with nouns?

trip.prompt: Read about the ageing population and list two vocabulary items from the page.

stages.title: Academic language
stages.hook: In a Japanese academic paper, "I think" becomes "it is thought". Why does the author step back?
explain: Academic Japanese uses the である style and an impersonal tone. 仮説 (kasetsu, hypothesis), 先行研究 (senkō kenkyū, previous research), 結果 (kekka, results), 考察 (kōsatsu, discussion) and 引用 (in'yō, citation) are standard. 本稿 (honkō) means this paper.

To hedge, writers use 〜と考えられる (it can be considered that), 〜と言える (it can be said that), 〜可能性がある (there is a possibility) and 〜に関して (regarding). The passive and potential forms make the claim less personal. Strong claims need evidence.

Structure: introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion and references. 先行研究を踏まえて (based on previous studies) shows you know the field. Quote carefully with 「 」 and a source. Copying without a source is plagiarism (剽窃, hyōsetsu).
stages.mnemonic: である style, impersonal voice, hedged claims.
sentences: From this result, the following can be said.

gq.why: 〜と考えられる makes a claim less direct.

o: A conclusion at the end of a paper
A style used for citing sources
gq.why: It means previous research in the field.

panel.q: Why does academic Japanese avoid 私は思う?
panel.why: An impersonal tone is preferred to sound objective.

panel.q: A writer copies a paragraph without quotation or source. What is this?
panel.why: Using someone's words without credit is plagiarism.

panel.q: Which section interprets the results?
panel.why: 考察 is the discussion section.

teach.model: Academic Japanese uses the である style, an impersonal voice and hedges such as ~to kangaerareru. It builds on previous research and cites sources to avoid plagiarism.

points.ask: What must I do with others' work?

trip.prompt: Read about academic writing and identify hedging in an example.

stages.title: Professional communication
stages.hook: In a Japanese office, why do people say ほうれんそう? It is not a vegetable here.
explain: Workplace Japanese is polite and precise. 会議 (kaigi, meeting), 議事録 (gijiroku, minutes), 締め切り (shimekiri, deadline), 取引先 (torihikisaki, client) and 確認 (kakunin, confirmation) are common. Business phrases include 恐れ入ります (osore irimasu, sorry to trouble you) and 承知しました (understood).
ほうれんそう (報連相) stands for 報告 (report), 連絡 (contact) and 相談 (consult). It is a workplace habit of keeping your supervisor informed. The word also sounds like spinach, which makes it easy to remember.

Business cards (名刺, meishi) are exchanged with both hands, with a small bow, and the card is read carefully, not put away immediately. Requests are softened: 会議の資料をご確認ください (please check the meeting materials). Use sonkeigo for clients and kenjōgo for yourself.
stages.mnemonic: ほうれんそう: report, contact, consult.
sentences: I hand over the business card with both hands.

gq.q: What does ほうれんそう stand for?
o: Rice, bread and tea served at lunch
Read, write and speak in the office
Plan, do and check each project
gq.why: It abbreviates report, contact and consult.

gq.q: How should you exchange a business card?
o: With one hand while looking away
By putting it in a pocket at once
gq.why: Customarily with both hands and a slight bow.

panel.q: Why is 恐れ入ります used before a request?
panel.why: It softens the request and shows respect.

panel.q: A junior colleague finds a problem and tells nobody. What principle is broken?
panel.why: Reporting early is the point of ほうれんそう.

panel.q: Which pair is correct in a client meeting?
o: Humble for the client, honorific for yourself
Honorific for the client, humble for yourself
panel.why: Use honorific for the client's actions and humble for yours.

teach.model: Offices value reporting, contacting and consulting: ほうれんそう. Business cards are given with both hands, and requests are softened with phrases like 恐れ入ります. Use keigo for clients.

points.ask: What does ほうれんそう mean?
How do I give a business card?
How should I speak to clients?

trip.prompt: Read about meishi etiquette and list two rules.

stages.title: Literary analysis
stages.hook: A cherry blossom falls in a poem. Is it about flowers, or about the passing of time?
explain: Literary analysis asks about 主題 (shudai, theme), 語り手 (katarite, narrator), 比喩 (hiyu, metaphor), 象徴 (shōchō, symbol), 情景 (jōkei, scene), 文体 (buntai, style) and 余韻 (yoin, lingering effect). In Japanese literature, nature images often carry emotion.

The 『源氏物語』 (The Tale of Genji), attributed to Murasaki Shikibu (紫式部) in the early 11th century, is often called one of the world's earliest novels. The opening of 『平家物語』 (The Tale of the Heike) reads 祇園精舎の鐘の声、諸行無常の響きあり: the bell of Gion Shōja has the sound of impermanence (無常, mujō).

Cherry blossoms (桜) commonly symbolise the beauty and brevity of life, but a symbol is not fixed: a reader must check context. Notice the narrator, the sentence endings and the season words, and avoid claiming a single "correct" reading.
stages.mnemonic: Image, symbol, theme: ask what the image carries.
sentences: The author expresses impermanence with cherry blossoms.
I pay attention to the narrator's viewpoint.
This style leaves a lingering resonance.

gq.q: Who is traditionally credited with writing The Tale of Genji?
gq.why: Murasaki Shikibu is credited with the Genji.

panel.q: What do cherry blossoms often symbolise?
o: Money and good luck in business deals
The beauty and brevity of life
War and the soldiers who fight it
panel.why: They often symbolise the beauty and brevity of life.

panel.q: Why should a reader avoid claiming a single correct reading?
o: Texts have no meaning beyond the words
Poems are not literature, so they have no readings
Only the author knows the true reading
panel.why: Symbols depend on context, and several interpretations are possible.

panel.q: What does a 語り手 influence?
o: The font of the printed book
The paper the book is printed on
panel.why: The narrator shapes the viewpoint of the story.

teach.model: To analyse a text, look at theme, narrator, images and style. Nature images often carry emotion, such as cherry blossoms for the brevity of life. Context controls the reading.

points.ask: What do cherry blossoms often mean?

trip.prompt: Read the summary of The Tale of Genji and note why it is important.

stages.title: Advanced listening comprehension
stages.hook: A speaker says 検討してみます in a calm voice. Is that a yes? Listening between the lines matters.
explain: Advanced listening means following ニュース (news), 講義 (kōgi, lectures) and meetings. Look for the 論点 (ronten, point at issue) and the speaker's structure: 前置き (maeoki, preamble), main point, example and conclusion. Take notes with key words only.

Meaning beyond the words (含み, fukumi) is common. 検討してみます (I will consider it) can be a polite way of not agreeing. 難しいかもしれません (it may be difficult) often means no. Tone, pauses and hedges all matter. When unsure, ask politely: 聞き返す (kikikaesu) means to ask someone to repeat or clarify.
Practise by listening to news at normal speed, writing the main points, and checking against the transcript. Notice speed, dropped particles in casual speech and shortened forms like 食べてる (食べている).
stages.mnemonic: Gist first, then the hidden meaning.
sentences: I summarise the main points of the lecture in my notes.
When I do not understand, I ask again.

gq.why: It is an introductory remark before the main point.

gq.q: What may 検討してみます mean in business?
o: A firm yes that means a deal is made
A firm no, said with anger
A greeting for the start of a meeting
gq.why: It can be a noncommittal answer.

panel.q: Why take notes with key words only?
o: To copy everything the speaker says word for word
To avoid listening to the talk at all
To save time and keep the structure
panel.why: Key words save time and keep the structure clear.

panel.q: A colleague says 難しいかもしれません about your proposal. How should you read it?
o: A definite yes, so you can go ahead
A request for money to fund the plan
A greeting used at the start of a meeting
panel.why: Such hedged wording often signals a refusal.

panel.q: Why do news broadcasts help advanced learners?
o: Clear speech, varied vocabulary and transcripts
They use only kana, so they are easy to read
They are always spoken slowly for beginners
They contain no kanji, so they are easy
panel.why: They offer clear, formal speech on varied topics with transcripts available.

teach.model: In advanced listening, find the point at issue, follow the structure and listen for implications. Phrases like 検討してみます can be noncommittal. Ask politely if unsure.

trip.prompt: Read about indirect speech and find an example in another language.

stages.title: Oral fluency and presentations
stages.hook: A fluent speaker sounds natural not because of speed but because of pauses, paraphrase and clear structure.
explain: Fluency (流暢, ryūchō) in Japanese is about natural rhythm, not speed. A well-placed pause (間, ma) lets listeners follow. Fillers (フィラー) such as えーと and あのう are normal, but too many weaken the message. Intonation (抑揚) is gentle but the sentence-ending tone shows attitude.

言い換え (iikae, paraphrasing) helps when you cannot find a word: say it in simpler terms. In presentations, an outline at the start, a summary of key points (要約, yōyaku) and a question session (質疑応答, shitsugi ōtō) are standard. Persuasiveness (説得力, settokuryoku) comes from reasons and examples.
Practise by recording yourself, timing your talk and shadowing a model. Speak in the polite です・ます style unless the situation is casual. When you make an error, correct it calmly and keep going.
sentences: We will have a question and answer session.
I help my explanation by paraphrasing.

gq.q: What does 言い換え help with?
o: Counting the words in a speech
Greeting the audience at the start
gq.why: It helps explain an idea in other words.

gq.q: What is a 質疑応答?
o: A speech given at the start
A letter sent after a talk
A greeting used by the host
gq.why: It is a question and answer session.

panel.q: A speaker uses えーと every few words. What is the advice?
o: Use even more fillers to sound natural
Speak faster so nobody notices them
Stop speaking whenever you feel unsure
panel.why: Too many fillers weaken the message; use pauses instead.

panel.q: Why record your own speech?
o: To avoid having to practise aloud
To memorise kanji from the playback
To save space on the phone
panel.why: You can hear pace, pauses and errors.

panel.q: What gives a speech 説得力?
o: Speed, since fast talk sounds sure
Volume only, as loud talk persuades
panel.why: Clear reasons and examples make it persuasive.

teach.model: Fluency is about rhythm, pauses and clear structure. Paraphrasing helps when you lack a word. Presentations have an outline, a summary and a Q&A session.

points.ask: What if I lack a word?
What are standard parts of a presentation?

trip.prompt: Read about fluency and list two ways to measure it.

stages.title: Translation and interpretation
stages.hook: Is it harder to interpret live or to translate on paper? They are different skills.
explain: 通訳 (tsūyaku) is interpreting and 翻訳 (hon'yaku) is written translation. 逐次通訳 (chikuji tsūyaku) is consecutive interpreting: the speaker pauses and the interpreter speaks. 同時通訳 (dōji tsūyaku) is simultaneous: the interpreter speaks almost at the same time with headphones.

Japanese verbs come last, so interpreters into English often must wait for the end of the sentence or predict it. Interpreters use notes, shorten long sentences and keep numbers and names accurate. Confidentiality (守秘義務, shuhi gimu) is a professional duty.

Translators use a glossary (用語集, yōgoshū) to keep terms consistent. A second person proofreads (校閲, kōetsu). Handling keigo and omitted subjects requires judgement. Translation errors in legal or medical documents can be serious, so accuracy comes before style.
stages.mnemonic: Wait for the verb, then speak.
sentences: I unify the terms in the translation.
I keep the duty of confidentiality.

gq.why: In 逐次通訳 the speaker pauses for the interpreter.

gq.q: Why is the Japanese verb position a challenge for interpreters?
o: There are no verbs in Japanese
The verb comes first in the sentence
Verbs are always silent in speech
gq.why: The verb comes last, so the meaning may not be clear until the end.

panel.q: What is a glossary used for?
o: Counting the words in a text
panel.why: It keeps terminology consistent.

panel.q: An interpreter learns private information during a job. What is the duty?
o: Sell it to a news company
panel.why: 守秘義務 means keeping confidentiality.

panel.q: In legal translation, what comes first?
panel.why: Accuracy matters more than elegant style.

teach.model: Interpreting is spoken, translation is written. Simultaneous interpreting is almost live, and consecutive waits for pauses. The verb-final order is a challenge. Glossaries and confidentiality matter.

trip.prompt: Read about simultaneous interpreting and note one difficulty.

stages.title: Idiomatic and figurative language
stages.hook: "Kill two birds with one stone" in Japanese uses one stone and two birds too: 一石二鳥. Which other idioms have their own images?
explain: Japanese is rich in four-character idioms (四字熟語, yojijukugo) and proverbs (ことわざ, kotowaza). 一石二鳥 (isseki nichō) means one stone, two birds. 七転び八起き (nanakorobi yaoki) means fall seven times, get up eight: never give up. 十人十色 (jūnin toiro) means ten people, ten colours: everyone is different.

猫の手も借りたい (neko no te mo karitai) means so busy that you would even borrow a cat's paw. 花より団子 (hana yori dango) means dumplings over flowers: substance over appearance. 石の上にも三年 (ishi no ue ni mo sannen) means three years on a stone: patience brings results. 温故知新 (onko chishin) means learn from the old to know the new.
Idioms are fixed. Do not change the form or translate literally. Choose the idiom that matches the situation, and mind the tone: some are casual (猫の手も借りたい), some are formal (温故知新).
stages.mnemonic: Idioms are small pictures with a message.
items: so busy I'd borrow a cat's paw
ishi no ue ni mo sannen
sentences: This method kills two birds with one stone.
Ten people, ten colours, so opinions differ.
I try with a never-give-up spirit.

gq.why: 七転び八起き means to rise again after falling.

gq.q: Which idiom says everyone is different?
gq.why: 十人十色 means ten people, ten colours.

panel.q: A shop is extremely busy. Which idiom fits?
panel.why: 猫の手も借りたい describes being very busy.

panel.q: A student prefers snacks to the flower viewing. Which idiom fits?
panel.why: 花より団子 refers to preferring substance to appearance.

panel.q: Why not translate idioms word for word?
o: They have no meaning, only sounds
They are not Japanese at all, but Chinese
They change every day, like slang
panel.why: The meaning comes from the figure, not the literal words.

teach.model: Japanese idioms and proverbs use images to carry meaning. 一石二鳥 is two benefits at once, 七転び八起き is perseverance, and 猫の手も借りたい is being very busy. Use them in their fixed form.

trip.prompt: Pick an idiom from the page and write a sentence using it.

stages.title: Extended independent writing
stages.hook: You must write an essay of 800 characters. How do you plan a text that has a beginning, middle and end?
explain: A Japanese essay (小論文, shōronbun) often has 序論 (joron, introduction), 本論 (honron, body) and 結論 (ketsuron, conclusion). Another common structure for stories and some essays is 起承転結 (kishō tenketsu): introduction, development, twist, conclusion.

Use consistent style: である style for essays. Link ideas with connectors like まず, 一方 (on the other hand), したがって (therefore) and しかし (however). State a claim, give a reason, then an example. Vary sentence length, and avoid overly long chains with が and ので.

Revise (推敲, suikō) at the end. Check particles, verb endings, kanji and okurigana, punctuation, and that the style is unified. Reading aloud helps you find awkward phrases. A good style is clear first, graceful second.
stages.mnemonic: Plan, write, revise: 序論, 本論, 結論, 推敲.
sentences: First, I present the problem in the introduction.
In the body I state the evidence.
Finally, I revise and complete it.

gq.q: Which section states the final answer?

o: Starting to write the first draft
Reading it aloud and nothing else
gq.why: 推敲 means polishing a text through revision.

panel.q: Which connector marks a result or consequence?
panel.why: したがって means therefore.

panel.q: Why is style consistency important?
o: Style does not matter in an essay
Mixing is required to show skill
It changes the topic of the essay
panel.why: Mixing だ・である and です・ます in a text looks careless.

panel.q: A student writes one long sentence chained with ので and が. What is the advice?
o: Make it longer by adding more connectors
Remove all verbs to save space
Use only katakana to make it clear
panel.why: Shorter sentences and varied connectors improve clarity.

teach.model: A good essay has an introduction, body and conclusion, or kishō tenketsu. Use connectors, a consistent style and finish with revision.

points.ask: What do I do at the end?

trip.prompt: Compare jo-ha-kyū or kishōtenketsu with a Western essay plan.
